## Six years of packages, none of which come apart {visibility="uncounted"}

| Package | Since | Stars | Downloads |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EpiNow2` | 2020 | 141 | 58,073 |
| `epinowcast` | 2021 | 67 | not on CRAN |
| `epidist` | 2023 | 16 | not on CRAN |
| `primarycensored` | 2024 | 9 | 11,294 |
| `CensoredDistributions.jl` | 2024 | 15 | 122 |

- The same structural request has been written down in `EpiNow2` four
  times across five and a half years. **#122** (2020) and **#313** (2022)
  were closed as done and left the package no easier to take apart.
  **#1268** and **#1345** are still open
- Sharing a component between two Stan packages means copying its source
  in. `epinowcast` carries `inst/stan/functions/primarycensored.stan`
  with `LICENSE.primarycensored` beside it, and **#1268** asks `EpiNow2`
  to do the same

## A live outbreak, and four questions I cannot answer {visibility="uncounted"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
**Where we have got to**

![](../figures/bvd-outbreak-streams.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Posterior densities for cumulative infections, one curve per
data stream and one for the joint fit, which sits inside the spread of
the single-stream fits."}

- The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic
  of the Congo, fitted in Julia. One renewal model over the suspected,
  confirmed, death, export and bed-occupancy counts, fitted together
- Mooncake differentiates all of it. Enzyme matches Mooncake to 4e-15 on
  a single stream and cannot compile the joint
- Over 30,000 lines of Julia for one outbreak, most of it written by
  agents

**What holds the packages together**

- `EpiAwarePackageTools.jl` writes 78 template files into each package,
  including nine quality checks that run as tests
- Seven autodiff configurations in one list, six of them running in every
  package
- 22 reusable workflows in one `.github` repository, each caller pinned
  to a commit SHA

::: {.attribution}
[BVDOutbreakSize](https://github.com/epiforecasts/BVDOutbreakSize), the
`bvd_joint` arguments and the Julia line count read 2026-08-12 · the
Enzyme comparison is
[BVDOutbreakSize#445](https://github.com/epiforecasts/BVDOutbreakSize/issues/445),
open at 2026-08-12 · `templates/`, `src/scaffold.jl` and
`templates/test/package/quality.jl` in
[EpiAwarePackageTools.jl](https://github.com/EpiAware/EpiAwarePackageTools.jl)
at commit `427d4f5`, read 2026-08-12 · 22 of the 23 workflows in
[EpiAware/.github](https://github.com/EpiAware/.github) declare
`workflow_call`, from the contents API 2026-08-13
:::
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**What we cannot answer**

1. What is the smallest governance you can start with? JuMP and SciML
   have written theirs. Turing has not. None of them says how an org
   starts, or how a package joins one
2. Julia has no rOpenSci. Should it? No maintenance status labels, no
   disputes procedure. How do I decide whether to depend on a
   one-maintainer package?
3. Who tells a user which backend works for a model built from five
   packages? DifferentiationInterface answers for a function. Nothing
   composes
4. How do you release eleven packages that have to work together? SciML
   runs downstream CI outside its own org, as workflow files rather than
   guidance, and nothing publishes a tested version set

::: {.callout-important}
And the one behind all of them. Is there a Julia ecosystem whose users
are mostly not developers? I went looking and could not find one.
:::

`EpiAwareR`, Sebastian Funk's R interface prototype, is our attempt at
that question. It is the piece I am least sure how to sustain.
:::
